title: capture-profiles-v1
description: The publisher capture registry. Pure data: one set of selectors read by the browser extension, by an acquisition script and by a receiver's mapping, so a selector never has to be fixed in three places. `status` is a measurement, not a plan.

status_meanings.description: What each status claims, written down so the registry explains its own vocabulary.

genericProfile.description: The fallback. It claims no hosts and has no status: it is what runs when nothing matched, and a publisher profile inherits from it whatever it does not override.

host_patterns.description: Hosts this profile claims. A leading `*.` matches the bare domain and any subdomain.

article_container_selectors.description: Where the article body is. Serializing the whole document is what carries the adverts, the modals and the marketing rails into the artifact.

figure_selectors.description: The publisher's own figure elements. Rung 1 of structural figure selection.

access_markers.description: What the page shows a reader without entitlement. An observation, never a licence.

status.description: supported = a committed fixture exists and a test asserts container, identity and the figure manifest against it. generic = only the fallback selectors are proven. unsupported = something was measured and it did not work.

fixture.description: Repository path to the skeleton fixture that proves `supported`. Dropped from the projection served to the extension, which must carry no repository paths.

reason.description: Required when status is unsupported: what was OBSERVED, not what is assumed.

asset_origins.description: Hosts other than the page's own origin that this publisher serves assets from. A leading `*.` matches the bare domain and any subdomain. Anything not the page origin and not on this list is never fetched; anything that is not the page origin is fetched without the reader's cookies.
